title: Art That Speaks Up: A New Show Lets Prints Do the Talking
summary: What if a piece of paper could shout, whisper, or sing about important things? At a new art show in Philadelphia, that's exactly what's happening. The Print Center is hosting 'America Today: Voices in Contemporary Print,' an exhibition where artists use printmaking—a way of creating art by pressing ink onto paper—to share their thoughts on big topics like civil rights, social justice, and community stories. The show runs until July 25 and features 37 artists from all over the United States. The artworks come from six special printmaking workshops that are more than just studios—they're places where artists gather, support each other, and speak up about what matters to them. Some prints are colorful and bold, while others are quiet and detailed. They touch on everything from personal histories to political actions. You might see a print about a local hero, a protest, or a cultural tradition. The artists include Natalie Ball, Chakaia Booker, and Howardena Pindell, among many others. The exhibition is part of the nation's 250th anniversary, but it's not just about celebrating—it's about asking questions. What kind of country do we want to be? How can art help us understand each other better? If you're in Philadelphia, stop by and let these prints speak to you. You might just hear something surprising!
why_it_matters: Art can help you understand other people's experiences and think about how to make your own community better.

background_read: Printmaking is an art form where an artist creates an image on a block or screen and then transfers it onto paper, so many copies can be made.
The Print Center in Philadelphia is a museum that has been showing print art for over 100 years.
The United States celebrated its 250th birthday in 2026, and this exhibition is part of that celebration, asking people to think about the country's past and future.
